figure: Figure 8.1 (Where inference computation and data movement actually live)
issue: The figure's structure visually contradicts its central conceptual claim and requires the long caption to rescue it. The caption explicitly says 'compute, memory and interconnect are separate groups in this figure, not levels of one ladder' and 'only the memory hierarchy is a smallest-to-largest ladder'. Yet all seven boxes are stacked in a single column with uniform inter-box connector marks, so at a glance the layout reads as one 7-rung hierarchy — with the blue 'tensor cores / ALU' (compute) box as a rung between registers and shared memory, and the two green interconnect boxes as the bottom rungs. The red gradient arrow is correctly scoped to the memory group (registers→HBM), but the chain connectors and single-column layout still imply a continuous ladder across all three groups. Per the standard 'if prose is required to rescue an ambiguous diagram, improve the diagram', the figure should carry the 'three distinct groups' point on its own.
evidence: Caption clauses: 'not levels of one ladder' and 'only the memory hierarchy is a smallest-to-largest ladder'. Rendered layout: one vertical column, small connector marks between every adjacent pair of boxes (including registers↔tensor cores and HBM↔GPU interconnect), no visual grouping/bracket separating the blue compute box or the green interconnect boxes from the orange memory stack.
acceptance_test: Redesign so the three categories are visually distinct without reading the caption: e.g., place the compute box in its own column/side position, add clear group separators or brackets around {memory hierarchy}, {compute}, {interconnect}, remove the uniform chain connectors between groups (keep them only within the memory stack), and keep the red capacity/speed/distance arrow spanning the memory group only. Confirm a reader who sees only the figure (not the caption) infers three groups, not one 7-level ladder.
